name: Dim Grey
lede: Dim Grey is a neutral mid-dark grey from the X11 color list, exactly 105 on each of red, green and blue.

sections.title: A listed color
sections.body:
Paterson's dictionary lists DimGray as an entry in the X11 Color Set, with hex code 696969 [1]. Each pair of digits is 69 in hex, which is 105 on the 0 to 255 scale, so the three channels are equal and the color has no hue [5]. In ordinary language, Paterson defines dim as poorly lit, or lacking lustre or brilliance [1]. His index files it among the greys [2]. Our name records list CSS, a web encyclopedia and RAL (1927) [3].

Its nearest neighbors among our names, by CIELAB distance, are [[deep-neutral-grey|Deep Neutral Grey]], [[nickel|Nickel]] and [[slate-grey|Slate grey]] [5]. On a white page it reaches a contrast ratio of 5.49:1 [5].

sections.title: In paintings
sections.body: Dim Grey is one of the most common named colors in our archive: it appears in 457 of 23,781 paintings, 1.92%, more often than 73% of the named colors [4]. It most often plays a light, in 35% of the 231 paintings where the within-painting reading finds it [4]. It peaks in the 1900s at 1.6 times the expected rate [4]. Matisse painted it most often (4 of his 50 works here), though no painter stands out against the museum baseline [4]. It is most over-represented in Norway, at 3.2 times expected (7 of 120 paintings) [4].
